content.thinking:
I'm going for a Blizzard/Warcraft-inspired hand-painted heroic style, using painted gradients, bark texture, and glowing eyes/runes rather than flat toon shading. For the design, I'm settling on an ancient treant roughly 4.5 meters tall, scaled down from Warcraft's towering Ancient of War.

Now I'm planning the skeleton: a thick-trunked pelvis and spine rising into a chest, neck, and head, with oversized shoulders and massive root-fingered arms held in an A-pose, plus thick root-legs ending in spreading toe-roots for feet. The face is carved into the trunk with a separate jaw joint, glowing eyes, mossy brow, and a crown of branches on top.

For the crown, I'm adding leaf clusters, antler-like branches, a bird's nest with eggs, mushrooms on the shoulders, hanging vines, glowing amber sap, carved glowing runes on the chest, and a rusted hatchet embedded in the shoulder with a vine wrapped around it for a bit of backstory, plus buttress roots spreading from the feet into the ground. I need to keep this within a 1000-part, 60k-triangle budget, and now I'm working out a custom bark paint combining vertical grain streaks, bark-plate scaling, and moss countershading on the upward-facing surfaces.

Writing bark paint function...

I'm sizing the paint texture — figuring the creature's painted surface area needs roughly 2048px resolution to keep texel density fine enough for the crevice details without wasting atlas space, and all parts will share a single material. Now I'm sketching out the actual geometry coordinates, orienting the model so it faces +Z with +X to the left.

I'm working out the leg proportions and joint chain — hip joints placed symmetrically with thick trunk-like radii, feet positioned below, and laying out the limb chain names for hip, knee, and ankle joints plus the tip for each leg.

For the foot, I'm planning a wide flattened base mass with spreading toe chains fanning outward from the ankle, using thin radius sprouts with bent tips to suggest claws or roots.

Checking the hip-to-ankle geometry, I'm working out whether leg segments of 0.95 and 0.8 can reach the ankle target with the hips at a given height, adjusting coordinates slightly so the knee has a natural bend rather than being nearly straight.

Now I'm laying out the torso as a lofted shape from pelvis to neck, defining widths and heights at each station—pelvis, waist, chest, shoulders, and neck—to give the treant a broad, tapering build.

I'll have the trunk lean forward slightly for a hunched heroic pose, curving from pelvis to chest to neck base, with oversized gnarled burl-like pauldrons at the shoulders for that bark-painted heroic look. I'm setting the trunk radius to 0.55 for a sturdy build.

For the arms, I'm scaling shoulders broad at roughly 2.2 meters with the burls, running shoulder-elbow-wrist joints with tapering radii and thicker mallet-like forearms. I'm making the hands oversized with a palm sphere plus four jointed fingers and a thumb, positioning them so fingertips hang just above the ground without touching it.

Setting overall height around 4.6 meters, I'm building the head as a large burl-textured skull with heavy brow ridge, branch-stub nose, glowing amber eyes in dark sockets, a separate jaw with mossy beard and splinter-like wooden teeth, bark-ridge lips, and shelf-fungus ears, plus mossy twig-tuft eyebrows for facial detail. Now I'm starting on the crown structure branching up from the top of the head.

Planning 5-6 thick jointed branches sweeping up like antlers with sub-twigs and leaf cards, plus leaf clusters on shoulders and back using oak-like textures in Ashenvale-style greens with golden-orange accents, against a palette of brown-violet bark, ochre highlights, moss green, and glowing amber eyes/runes. I'm also adding backstory details: a rusted axe embedded in the shoulder, an elf-cut scar, glowing mushrooms, a bird's nest with blue eggs in the crown, hanging vines with flowers, and a glowing amber spiral rune on the chest with sap trailing down.

For asymmetry I'm putting ivy wrapping the right forearm, a stone lodged in the roots, and bark-armor plates with Warcraft-style rivets and worn trim, plus a braided vine belt with a bronze druidic disc buckle and bronze wrist bands — keeping the axe on the left shoulder and ivy on the right arm as a storytelling contrast. Now I'm shifting into the technical implementation, working through the chain/sweep API for generating the branch geometry and figuring out how to loft the torso shape.

Defining the color palette and paint values...

Writing bark paint function...

Adding bark coloring and shading...

I'll also blend in dirt tones near the base of the trunk, and need to check that the paint function's return type works cleanly with the mix operations. Performance-wise, with per-texel noise evaluation across a large texture sheet this could take a few seconds, which seems acceptable to try. I'm planning out separate paint variants for different parts: body bark, limb bark, roots (darker), head (lighter and warmer with less moss), palms, and a dedicated moss paint.

For the hand-painted Warcraft-style look I want baked ambient occlusion — darkening lower areas and crevices based on height and normal direction. Now I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy, working out the hips joint as root and the spine chain with named segments branching upward, making sure the point counts match up with the joint names correctly.

Still defining spine and neck joints...

I'll just sweep the torso along the spine chain, since hips and spine1 share the same start point, and add pelvis lumps as spheres near the hips. For the radius profile, I'm thinking of a wide chest tapering toward the shoulders as the path parameter moves from pelvis upward.

Defining torso radius profile...

I'm also planning bark surface details—chunky bark plate shards scattered on the torso and vertical root-like buttress ridges made from thin sweep tubes placed at multiple angles with slight moss accents.

For the arms, I'm setting up a chain structure with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints parented to the chest, with shoulder burls positioned slightly outward on either side.

Now I'm calculating the limb geometry — working out shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions and computing the upper arm and forearm lengths from the coordinates, so the elbows bend backward naturally.

With shoulder around 3.3, wrist lands at 1.45 and fingertips extend down to about 0.75, giving that heroic gorilla-like reach. I'm sizing arm thickness with a tapering radius from upper arm to forearm to wrist, then shaping hands as box-ish palms hanging down with fingers oriented along the tangent at the wrist joint.

Now I'm planning finger chains: four fingers plus thumb per hand, each with knuckle and tip joints curving slightly forward for a claw-like look, giving 20 finger joints total across both hands. Adding toes similarly brings 16 more joints, and with roughly 24 branch joints for the crown plus jaw, I'm tallying everything against the 160 joint budget to make sure it fits.

I'm defining the taper on each finger from thick base to pointy bark-colored tip, then positioning the hands so palms face inward with fingers curling downward and slightly forward relative to the wrist, calculating knuckle, mid, and tip coordinates as offsets from the wrist position.

I still need to parent the finger chains to the wrist joint and figure out naming conventions, then move on to building the leg chains from the hips down through knees to ankle targets, parented at the hips with a "leg" role.

Now I'm defining the leg bone radii tapering from thigh to ankle, then building the foot as a mass sphere with four toe chains sprouting forward and slightly down from the ankle, tapering in radius and sinking just below ground level at the tips for a grounded look.

I need to double-check that the lowest contact points—toe tips and a heel path extending back from the ankle—actually touch the floor within a reasonable tolerance, adjusting cap radii and endpoint heights as needed, and I'm also planning thick snaking root shapes rigidly attached to each foot that wiggle outward across the ground using catmull curves.

I'm sketching the legs as two trunks fused at the hips with flared, root-like bases—adding a flattened ellipsoid at each ankle to form a foot-mass that sits just above the floor, and treating the overall limb as a swept shape with varying radii, while the pelvis forms a skirt-like sweep that transitions into the torso starting around hip height.

Now I'm checking the pelvic width against the torso radius to make sure the legs meet cleanly at the hips, then planning a vine-textured belt that loops around the waist with a bronze buckle disc on the front, figuring out how to orient the buckle so it faces forward using a surface ray cast to find the correct position and normal on the torso.

For the chest, I want a glowing rune decal where only the amber stroke lines emit light while the rest stays transparent, possibly layering a darker, non-glowing outline beneath the amber lines to give the rune a carved-groove look.

Now I'm planning the head details for a readable 3/4 view: positioning a heavy angled brow ridge, dark eye sockets with protruding glowing amber orbs (plus a darker pupil disc for contrast), and starting to shape a gnarled branch-stub nose.

I'm continuing to block out the lower face — snub nose with twig sprout, cheek burls, and the jaw structure built from frustum boxes hinged forward. I'm adding a dark mouth cavity gap between the jaws and planning two upward tusk-like protrusions from the lower jaw for that chunky heroic Warcraft look, before moving on to the beard.

I'm sketching the beard with hanging moss cards and root-tendril spikes forming a goatee, shelf-fungus ears on either side of the head, and antler-crown "hair." For the skull itself I'm thinking of a scaled sphere with slab-like forehead geometry and a heavy brow, aiming for a wide flat face that reads clearly from the front, all rigged to a head bone positioned above the neck.

I decide to oversize the head a bit for a heroic look, scaling it to roughly 1.0 wide by 0.9 tall relative to the body, pushing the total figure height to about 5 meters including the crown branches sprouting from the top of the skull. I'm now setting up seven antlers radiating from the skull's crown point at varying azimuths.

For the branches themselves, I'm planning curved multi-joint paths growing up and outward, around 0.9-1.2 units long, using a sprout-chain approach and leaning toward the "tentacle" role since it best fits their flexible, limb-like nature. For foliage, I want to scatter leaf-textured card clusters across each branch sweep, around 40 per branch at a small size with some lean variation for a natural look.

I'm also adding sub-twig stubs that spike off the branch surfaces along the normal direction, keeping them bare since the leaf scatter already covers visual density, and planning dedicated foliage branches growing from the shoulder burls and back to give the treant a classic leafy canopy silhouette, with two prominent branches rising from the shoulders as the main visual anchors.

I'm working out the rig attachments for these parts — deciding the shoulder burls should bone-parent to the shoulder joint (acting like a pauldron riding the arm) rather than the chest, so their sprouted branches inherit that same parent, while the arms and neck chains both parent to the chest tip joint of the spine.

Now I'm sketching the torso chain itself as spine1/spine2/spine3/chest spans, and thinking through secondary decorations: hanging vines swept along the arms with leaf cards, mossy beards on the forearms, and mushrooms built from lathe-profile caps with cylinder stalks and painted white spots scattered across the shoulders and back.

An embedded rusted axe in the left shoulder adds character—iron blade from an extruded outline with rust mottling, wooden handle wrapped in tiny leather strips, angled outward with vines growing over it. I'm keeping it simple: skip extra arrows, just the axe plus a small bird's nest with eggs tucked into the crown.

Also considering a tiny wren perched on the right shoulder for whimsy—body sphere, head, beak cone, tail wedge, flattened wing spheres, around 8 parts total. For the back, I want bark plating, root-like ridges, moss, and a hollow with mushrooms to balance the front detail.

I'll keep the hollow simple as a dark ellipsoid disc rather than adding glow effects. At the base, roots will snake outward from the ankles across the floor using catmull curves with random wiggle, tapering from thick to thin. I'm also adding bronze wrist cuffs as tube rings swept along the forearm, with small rivets spaced along them.

I'm thinking through more bronze accents now: wide bracers made of thin loops and rivets, a belt buckle with a carved rune, and leg bands at the knee. I'll skip the hanging amulet and instead focus on an axe-scar detail -- a lopped-off branch stump on the arm showing pale cut wood rings, rendered as a flat disc with painted growth rings.

For the stumps I'll use a circle geometry textured with concentric tree-ring patterns, placed on three spots -- the torso sides and the right upper arm -- facing outward. I'm also planning thin glowing amber veins along surface cracks, like magical sap lines sweeping from the chest rune outward, to give it that nature-magic feel. Before writing the full code I want to double check the sweep/drape API signatures so I build everything correctly in one pass.

Now I'm sketching out leaf textures as SVGs with gradients -- a pointed green-to-gold oak-style leaf with vein lines and a darker outline, sized so the strokes stay crisp, plus moss tufts and ivy shapes for variety.

I'll also need interpolation helpers to compute radius profiles for the tube sweeps, then start setting up the import structure for the builder and frame modules.

Writing bark paint function...

Blending in the crack color, then adding a moss layer using noise influenced by the surface normal, making sure the color mixing types work properly throughout.

Computing moss amount via smoothstep on a noise-based value, coloring between dark and light moss tones, and darkening the base toward dirt near the ground. I'm also adding a height-based ambient occlusion factor to deepen shadows lower on the surface.

Thinking through torso and limb painting using the same bark function, with a slightly warmer, lighter variant for the head, and applying bark with dirt blending for roots touching the floor. I'm weighing the compute cost of painting at 2048² resolution with multiple noise octaves per texel, and deciding to try 1024 first to check performance before committing to a larger texture size.

Now I'm starting to build the actual skeleton code: setting up the builder with a paint size, seeding the RNG, and defining the hip joint and spine chain using a catmull-rom curve through four points to form the pelvis-to-chest hierarchy.

Jaw joint hangs off the head, aimed slightly down and forward. Now I'm sweeping the torso profile along the spine chain, parameterizing width and depth by position along the length.

Mapping torso height from waist to shoulders, I'm plotting width and depth values at keyframes so the silhouette narrows at the waist and widens toward the shoulders, with the top radius tucked under where the neck and shoulder burls will cover it.

I'm adding pectoral and shoulder burl spheres to give the torso a muscular, bark-like Warcraft aesthetic, then building the arm chains symmetrically for left and right sides. Writing arm chain code...

Adjusting the radius keys for the elbow bulge, then building the palm geometry attached to the wrist bone, positioning it slightly below and forward of the joint.

Now I'm working through finger placement—with arms hanging at the sides, palms naturally face the thighs, so the fingers should spread front-to-back rather than side-to-side. I'm reconsidering hand orientation for silhouette readability from the front, since a palm-inward pose would show only the hand's thin edge.

Still positioning finger segments...

Still defining leg and foot geometry...

Then I'll add root sweeps along the floor extending outward from under the feet, with tapering radius for a natural grounding effect.

I'm distributing root angles around the back and sides of each foot, avoiding the toe direction. Now moving to the head and neck structure, starting with the skull as a scaled sphere, then I'll add jaw and beard details.

Working out positions for brow ridges, eye sockets, and other facial features...

Still working out placement...

Styling nose as a knotty branch stub with bark texture and pale cut end, then placing cheek burls as sphere stubs, and adding an upper jaw block beneath the nose to suggest a maxilla shape.

Now I'm working out the lower jaw geometry, lofting a tapered box from the jaw pivot down to the chin so it sits slightly sunken, and adding a dark mouth cavity box tucked between the upper lip and jaw to read as the open mouth interior.

I'm calculating where the skull ellipsoid's underside meets the jaw at z=0.9, working through the cross-section math to get the upper lip level around y=3.79, then sizing the lower jaw frustum so its top edge just touches at 3.81, leaving a thin dark line for the mouth seam.

Now I'm sketching out the mouth line curve across the jaw, then planning tusks as upward-pointing cones placed at jaw hit points, plus smaller rows of teeth along the lower lip, and starting to think through how to attach beard-like moss tendrils sweeping down from several chin positions.

For the beard I'm defining bezier sweep paths from chin points downward and slightly forward, varying tendril lengths with a longer central goatee strand, capped with leaf and moss tuft cards. I'm also planning the crown area with sprouts, ear-shelf fungi, and scattered moss cards across the skull top, and mapping out base hit points for crown branches at specific azimuth/elevation angles around the head.

For each crown branch I'm computing outward-curving catmull-rom paths from the hit point with tapering radii, then scattering leaf cards across the sprout's surface using randomized directional flow so leaves face varied sides, and adding twig spikes along the sweep.

For leaf density I'm building clusters of cards at the twig tips using a ring arrangement rather than scattering, giving fuller tufts. Now I'm figuring out where to place the nest -- thinking of a flat shelf-like area near the fork or back-left crown.

Actually I'm reconsidering placement: putting the axe on the left shoulder, a bird and mushrooms on the right, and the nest centered at the skull top between the antlers, built as a lathed bowl shape with twigs swept around the rim, three eggs, and tiny leaves. I need to check the elevation so it doesn't collide with the central crown branch, so I'm adjusting its angle to sit just off-center.

For the bird I'm placing it on the right shoulder burl, composed of a scaled body sphere, head sphere, beak cone, tail, flat wings, eyes, and tiny feet, colored like a bright jay with cream belly to fit the stylized look.

For the axe, I'm figuring out where it embeds into the left shoulder burl, then working out the handle direction and blade orientation so the blade appears lodged in the wood with the handle projecting outward at an angle, defining the blade outline in the plane formed by the handle direction and cutting edge.

I need the blade edge buried into the shoulder, so C should point inward toward the surface while the handle extends outward and upward from the back of the head, with the edge positioned inside along that inward direction.

Since the head's drawing axes probably need to be orthogonal to avoid skewing, I'm orthogonalizing the handle direction against the inward axis by subtracting its projection onto C, giving a clean perpendicular handle vector.

Working out the axe geometry: positioning the head slightly outward along the normal, defining the poll-to-edge span along the inward axis with a flare in the perpendicular direction, and anchoring the handle rod vertically at the poll.

I'm planning the material details now—mottled rust iron with a bright beveled edge, pale wood tones for the handle, and a few small decorative rivet bands wrapped around the shaft, plus a spiral vine wrap for extra detail. I also need to set up hit targets for shoulder burls, and I'm sketching a mushroom-generating function that builds a frustum stalk and a lathed cap attached via a bone.

For the mushroom caps I'm using a hemisphere geometry with painted cream spots and a darker gill disc underneath, scattering about eight of them across the shoulders, forearm, back, roots, and ear shelves, with three glowing blue ones near the feet for an Ashenvale feel. Now I'm figuring out how to wrap vines in a spiral path around the forearm by computing points along the arm's centerline.

Still working out the vine sweep...

For bronze trims, I'm planning a bracer loop around the forearm by sampling the bone chain at a point partway down and using its direction to orient the loop.

Since sweep orientation is ambiguous for a loop path, I'll go simpler: three stacked circular sweeps spaced apart to form a ribbed bronze bracer, then add a row of rivets along it.

For rivets, rather than spawning tons of individual sphere parts per bracer, I'll merge them into a single part per bone group, attaching to the correct joint (like elbowL for the forearm bracer) to keep the part count manageable.

The sweep should ride the path's bones with averaged skin weights, which should work fine for arm skinning on a smooth tube. I want to quickly check the sweep function signatures in builder.ts before committing, then write and typecheck. For rune decals, I'm thinking of an SVG rune circle applied via decal.

For the chest, I'll add burls as small spheres on the pecs plus bark-ridge sweeps along the torso. Rather than straight regular lines, I want wiggly draped paths generated from catmull curves with random offsets at varying clock angles, so the ridges feel organic.

I'm computing twelve ridges of six points each, draping them onto the torso surface with slight wobble, then layering moss on top and scattering burl spheres for knots. For the armor-like texture, I'll scatter flattened box plates across the torso with random rotation, oriented so they shingle downward like bark plates.

Similar shingled plates will cover the legs and arms, following the downward flow of each limb, while I budget the total part count to stay around 400-600 for performance. I'm also planning moss tufts as small green grassy cards scattered on the shoulder tops, using a simple tuft SVG, and starting to think about adding flowers next.

Writing leaf gradient SVG path...

Adding more leaf variants...

Adding stump geometry and placement...

Now I'm settling the sign convention: azimuth 90 degrees corresponds to +X, treated as the left side, so I'll multiply azimuth by s directly for absolute coordinates. Time to write out the full file, handling jaw loft and head parts along with sphere geometries for other body pieces.

I'm defining a shared helper for creating parts with glow wrappers, then planning the build order from skeleton to torso, head, arms, and legs, keeping a consistent bark-textured paint across torso and limbs so the surface cracks read as continuous, with a slightly warmer variant reserved for the head.

Now I'm scattering leaf clusters onto the branch surfaces using randomized hit points, then rendering them as leaning, bending card geometry with varied scale and spin for a natural, wind-blown look.

Next I'm working through arm details like forearm bracer loops built from surface sweeps, moving on to hand knuckle spheres and wrist bark ridges while skipping the heel.

For the torso I'm adding a dorsal ridge of leafy branches sprouting from the back and shoulders, forming a dense canopy-like "backpack" silhouette using multiple arcing branch paths.

I'm also designing a hip-level loincloth made of hanging moss and vine tendrils around the belt, spaced to drape over the thighs without fully occluding the legs, then moving on to defining the glowing eye spheres.

Now I'm setting up helper utilities: a vector constructor, a frame function for orienting leaf tips, and a key-interpolation helper for the torso radius profile, while planning to define the arm bones before adding shoulder burls.

Working through the ordering and joint definitions for the legs—hip, knee, ankle chains with tapering radius profiles for thigh and calf, plus target positions and segment lengths for the leg geometry, alongside knee guard decorations and bark plate details for the lower body.

Checking that the leg's overall reach fits within the allowed limb length, I'm setting up the foot as a scaled sphere positioned at the ankle with a slight forward offset, then placing four toes fanned outward from the foot center with tapering radii and pointed caps, parented to the ankle chain, plus adding bronze knee band decorations at the leg joints.

Now I'm settling on paint details -- bark texture for the foot, pale spikes for toenails, and matching body paint for the hand parts. I'm also planning glowing veins draping from the chest rune outward across the torso and down one arm, plus a few small glowing forehead markings, before writing it all out and running a typecheck and preview.

input.command: ls samples | head -3; grep -n "scatter\|export type Hit\|stick(\|decal(" src/builder.ts | head -30; ls src
